description: v5. Each room's temperature comes from ONE resolved template sensor (sensor.climate_temp_<room>) that owns source priority, per-sensor bias and usability gating; the control loop, the dashboards and the floor/household averages all read it. The three bedrooms prefer their Tado TRV, falling back to the AC return-air probe when the valve is offline OR is driving the radiator, because a valve on a hot radiator reads high by an unmeasured amount. The HOUSE decides heat vs cool from the outdoor temperature (heat below / cool above, both global). Each ROOM has a day target and a night target — the temperature we are aiming to achieve — plus an optional air-filter mode that starts the unit at that target even when it has no thermal work to do. SAFETY (frost / away floor / away ceiling) runs even when the comfort master is off, and is gated as a whole by input_boolean.climate_safety_always, which is the one switch that disables every unconditional action. Manual changes at the wall are detected from a per-room command timestamp versus the unit's own last_changed, not from the failure counter. Commanded setpoints are rounded to whole degrees and clamped to the unit's own min_temp/max_temp. Wind-free presets are applied to COOLING ONLY - the units do not offer them in heat, and a preset sent to an off unit turns it on in cool.

actions.note: The room list is an explicit ALLOW-LIST OF ACTUATED ENTITIES: the only entity this automation ever passes to a climate.* service is r.climate, the room's Samsung AC. The gas boiler and its Tado valves are configured entirely outside it and are NEVER commanded here - the boiler is the winter failsafe and is not ours to drive. r.resolved and r.trv_watch are READ-ONLY: the resolved temperature is consumed as a sensor and the TRV setpoint is watched to verify the M6 invariant, but nothing is ever written to either. If you add a field here, check before use whether it is a read or a write.

variables.house: {% set prev = states('input_select.climate_house_mode') %}{% if outdoor <= -900 %}shoulder{% elif heat_below_out >= cool_above_out %}shoulder{% elif prev == 'heat' %}{% if outdoor > heat_below_out + hyst %}{% if outdoor >= cool_above_out %}cool{% else %}shoulder{% endif %}{% else %}heat{% endif %}{% elif prev == 'cool' %}{% if outdoor < cool_above_out - hyst %}{% if outdoor <= heat_below_out %}heat{% else %}shoulder{% endif %}{% else %}cool{% endif %}{% else %}{% if outdoor <= heat_below_out %}heat{% elif outdoor >= cool_above_out %}cool{% else %}shoulder{% endif %}{% endif %}

actions.note: HOUSE MODE is a property of the weather, not of a room, and it is now STICKY. Below 'heat below (outdoor)' the house heats; above 'cool above (outdoor)' it cools; between them is shoulder season, where nothing mechanical runs. EXIT-ONLY HYSTERESIS, the same shape every room already had. Entering a season uses the bare threshold; LEAVING it requires clearing the threshold by the hysteresis margin. Without this the boundary was a bare comparison with nothing damping it: on 2026-09-20 the outdoor reading sat at 17.3 C against a 17.0 C threshold, and a reading that wanders either side of the line would flip the whole house heat<->shoulder, taking every air-filter room with it, one cloud round trip per crossing. Every ROOM-level decision had hysteresis; the HOUSE-level one did not. The previous mode is remembered in input_select.climate_house_mode, whose options are ordered with 'shoulder' FIRST so that a freshly created or reset helper defaults to the season that does nothing - the same min-default hazard that put a bedroom 0.04 C from its safety floor. If the helper holds anything unexpected the expression falls through to the memoryless comparison, so a bad value costs stickiness and never correctness. It reuses climate_hysteresis rather than adding a knob: it is the same kind of quantity, a deadband in degrees. The coupling is real and deliberate - widening room hysteresis also makes the season stickier. If the outdoor sensor is unusable the house falls to SHOULDER rather than guessing a season, and an inverted band (heat_below >= cool_above) does the same. The safety band reads neither helper and keeps running regardless.

The house mode is written back ONLY when it changes, so this is not a write every tick. It is the state memory the exit-only hysteresis needs: rooms can use the unit's own reported mode as memory, but the house has no equivalent, so it keeps its own. Written after the decision, never read by anything except the decision above.

if.value_template: {% set ns = namespace(bad=false) %}{% for r in rooms %}{% if r.trv_watch != '' %}{% set sp = state_attr(r.trv_watch,'temperature') | float(0) %}{% set at = (states(r.night_t) if night else states(r.day_t)) | float(20) %}{% if sp > at %}{% set ns.bad = true %}{% endif %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{% set settle_bad = (states('input_number.climate_command_settle') | float(240)) < 60 %}{% set hyst_bad = (states('input_number.climate_hysteresis') | float(1)) < 0.5 %}{% set floor_bad = (states('input_number.climate_away_min') | float(18)) < 15 %}{% set frost_bad = (states('input_number.climate_frost_override') | float(7)) < 5 %}{% set trv_bad = (states('input_number.climate_trv_sensor_offset') | float(0) | abs) > 3 %}{% set ac_bad = (states('input_number.climate_ac_sensor_offset') | float(-2)) < -3.5 %}{{ heat_below_out >= cool_above_out or uptime > 34560000 or ns.bad or settle_bad or hyst_bad or floor_bad or frost_bad or trv_bad or ac_bad }}

data.title: Climate: configuration problem
data.message:
{% if heat_below_out >= cool_above_out %}**The house-mode band is inverted.** 'Heat below' ({{ heat_below_out }}) is not below 'Cool above' ({{ cool_above_out }}), so the house cannot resolve a season and ALL COMFORT HEATING AND COOLING IS STOOD DOWN. Only the safety band is still acting{% if not safety_on %} - and 'Safety limits always' is OFF, so NOTHING is protecting these rooms at all{% endif %}.

{% endif %}{% if uptime > 34560000 %}**The restart stamp is stale.** The guard that stops a post-restart fault being mistaken for someone at the wall is inert. Check automation.climate_stamp_ha_start.

{% endif %}{% for r in rooms %}{% if r.trv_watch != '' %}{% set sp = state_attr(r.trv_watch,'temperature') | float(0) %}{% set at = (states(r.night_t) if night else states(r.day_t)) | float(20) %}{% if sp > at %}**{{ r.name }}: the radiator valve is set above the room's current target** (TRV {{ sp }} C vs {{ 'night' if night else 'day' }} target {{ at }} C). The boiler and the AC will alternate. Set the TRV at or below {{ at }} C.

{% endif %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{% if (states('input_number.climate_command_settle') | float(240)) < 60 %}**Command settle is {{ states('input_number.climate_command_settle') }} s** - below 60 s our own in-flight commands read as unit faults.

{% endif %}{% if (states('input_number.climate_hysteresis') | float(1)) < 0.5 %}**Hysteresis is {{ states('input_number.climate_hysteresis') }} C** - below 0.5 C rooms will flap at their target.

{% endif %}{% if (states('input_number.climate_away_min') | float(18)) < 15 %}**The away floor is {{ states('input_number.climate_away_min') }} C** - that is below anything safe for the cats or the pipes. It should be about 18.

{% endif %}{% if (states('input_number.climate_frost_override') | float(7)) < 5 %}**The frost override is {{ states('input_number.climate_frost_override') }} C** - too low to protect plumbing.

{% endif %}{% if (states('input_number.climate_trv_sensor_offset') | float(0) | abs) > 3 %}**The TRV sensor offset is {{ states('input_number.climate_trv_sensor_offset') }} C.** That is far larger than any plausible radiator-valve bias, and it shifts the three bedrooms' temperature everywhere at once - the safety band, the graphs and the household average. A freshly created input_number comes up at its MINIMUM, which for this helper is -5: if that is what you are seeing, it was never set. It should be 0 until measured against a running radiator.

{% endif %}{% if (states('input_number.climate_ac_sensor_offset') | float(-2)) < -3.5 %}**The AC sensor offset is {{ states('input_number.climate_ac_sensor_offset') }} C** - larger than the measured return-air bias of about -2, and it corrupts every room that has fallen back to its AC probe.

{% endif %}

actions.note: Silent failure modes, all of which pass a float() guard because the value is REAL but wrong. (1) An inverted house band stands comfort down completely and composes with safety_always being off into a fully unprotected flat. (2) A stale restart stamp degrades unit_moved to its pre-v4.1 form. (3) M6: the AC and boiler only avoid fighting while each TRV setpoint stays at or below the room's CURRENT target - compared against day or night as actually in force (R7-5), since comparing always against the lower night target would flag a perfectly good daytime setting and train the operator to dismiss the notice. (4) R7-6, NUMERIC BOUNDS. A new input_number comes up at its MINIMUM, not zero - that already happened once here and put a bedroom 0.04 C from its safety floor. The same lands on any helper that is recreated or reset: away_min at its min of 5 would drop the cat floor to 5 C silently, settle below 60 s would make every one of our own commands read as a fault, hysteresis at 0 would make every room flap. float() catches non-numeric, never wrong-numeric, so these are range-checked. R8-4 extends the bounds check to the two CALIBRATION offsets, which is where the hazard actually bit: climate_trv_sensor_offset was created with min -5 and came up at -5.0, and -5.0 is INSIDE its valid range, so a range check alone would have passed it. These are therefore PLAUSIBILITY checks, not range checks - an offset is wrong long before it is out of bounds. They matter more since v5.1 because the offsets are applied inside the resolved template sensor, ahead of everything: a wrong offset moves the safety band, the dashboard and the household average from one place, and no guard further down the chain can see it. Checked and NOT added: breaker_threshold (helper min is 2, so the 0 that would re-open the A5 liveness trap is unreachable) and manual_hold_hours (min 0.5, not 0).

sequence.note: ONE RESOLVED TEMPERATURE PER ROOM, SHARED BY EVERYTHING. r.resolved is a template sensor (sensor.climate_temp_<room>) that owns the whole resolution: source priority, per-sensor bias, and the usability gates. The control loop, the dashboard graphs and the floor and household averages all read THAT SAME ENTITY, so they cannot disagree - and when a better sensor is added to a room, only that one template changes and every aggregate improves with it. It also makes the decision inspectable, which the design has wanted since section 13: the number the loop acted on is a real entity with history, not a variable that only exists inside a trace. Duplicating this logic here would create two implementations that drift, so the automation deliberately owns none of it and simply reads the result. If the sensor is unavailable or unknown it yields -999, which is the existing 'skip' sentinel: issue nothing, leave the room alone.

variables.manual_active: {{ manual_ts is not none and now().timestamp() < (manual_ts | float(0)) }}
variables.since_cmd: {{ (now().timestamp() - (cmd_ts | float(0))) if cmd_ts is not none else 999999 }}

sequence.note: since_cmd is how long ago WE last sent this room a command. With no stamp at all it is effectively infinite, which is correct: nothing of ours is in flight.

variables.unit_moved: {% set lc = (now() - states[r.climate].last_changed).total_seconds() %}{{ lc < since_cmd - settle and lc < human_window and lc < (uptime - 60) }}

sequence.note: THE IN-FLIGHT SIGNAL. in_flight says our own command has not had time to land; unit_moved says the unit changed state on its own, which only a person at the wall (or the unit acting by itself) can do. THE FIRST TERM IS 'lc < since_cmd - settle', NOT 'lc < since_cmd'. That subtraction is the whole point and its absence was a live bug on 2026-09-20. A unit that OBEYS us changes state about 1.5 s after we command it, so its last_changed is permanently a hair MORE RECENT than our command stamp - 'lc < since_cmd' is therefore true for ever after any successful command, not briefly. It stayed hidden because human_moved also needs 'not mode_ok', and a command that succeeded leaves the mode matching. The moment the WANTED mode changed for another reason - the operator switched the air filter off, so a room holding fan_only should go off - mode_ok went false while unit_moved was still true from our OWN earlier command. The automation stamped a two-hour manual hold on the Living room and pushed the operator a notification telling them they had changed a unit they had not touched. Subtracting settle asks the right question: did the unit change MORE THAN one cloud round trip after we commanded it? Our own command landing 1.5 s later cannot qualify; a person pressing a button minutes later always does. This is M1/R4-2 - the automation reading its own command as the unit's fault - for the third time, and the first time it has been the SUCCESSFUL command rather than an in-flight one. The remaining terms are unchanged: human_window bounds how stale a change can be and still count as a person, and lc < uptime - 60 stops a restart, which resets every entity's last_changed to the boot instant, from looking like everybody touched everything at once.

variables.mode: {% if temp <= -900 %}skip{% elif safety_on and temp < frost %}heat{% elif safety_on and temp < away_min %}heat{% elif safety_on and temp > away_max %}cool{% elif manual_active %}manual{% elif not comfort %}off{% elif away or not enabled %}off{% elif house == 'heat' %}{% if temp < target or (now_mode == 'heat' and temp < target + hyst) or filter_on %}heat{% else %}off{% endif %}{% elif house == 'cool' %}{% if temp > target or (now_mode == 'cool' and temp > target - hyst) or filter_on %}cool{% else %}off{% endif %}{% else %}{% if filter_on %}fan_only{% else %}off{% endif %}{% endif %}
variables.want_target: {% if safety_on and temp > -900 and temp < frost %}{{ frost }}{% elif safety_on and temp > -900 and temp < away_min %}{{ away_min }}{% elif safety_on and temp > -900 and temp > away_max %}{{ away_max }}{% else %}{{ target }}{% endif %}

sequence.note: Precedence: frost > away floor > away ceiling > manual hold > comfort. The three safety branches are now gated on safety_on, so input_boolean.climate_safety_always is a genuine master hatch for every unconditional action rather than a frost-only flag. AIR FILTER: when the house has a season but the room needs no thermal work, filter_on still starts the unit in that season's mode at the room's target (heat 22 in a 24 C room), which is what was asked for. In shoulder season it runs fan_only, the only mode that guarantees airflow with no thermal intent.

variables.set_target: {{ [[ (want_target | float(21)) | round(0) | int, umin | int ] | max, umax | int ] | min }}
variables.is_safety: {{ safety_on and temp > -900 and (temp < away_min or temp > away_max) }}

sequence.note: SETPOINT CLAMPING. The units report min_temp 16 / max_temp 30 / target_temp_step 1. A frost target of 7 C and any half-degree helper value are both setpoints the hardware cannot accept: it would silently keep its old value and every later tick would read as divergence. Every commanded setpoint is therefore rounded to a whole degree and clamped into the unit's own advertised range. The frost TRIGGER stays at 7 C; only the commanded setpoint is lifted to the unit's floor.

variables.target_ok: {{ (not needs_temp) or ((now_target | float(-1)) | round(0) | int) == set_target }}

variables.human_moved: {{ active and reachable and not mode_ok and not in_flight and unit_moved }}
variables.safety_throttled: {{ is_safety and manual_active and not throttle_ok }}

sequence.note: converged now covers the SETPOINT as well as the mode. A unit that accepts 'heat' but silently drops the setpoint used to look converged forever, so the breaker never tripped and nobody was told. It now counts as divergence and raises the same alert as a unit that ignores the mode.

variables.may_act: {{ active and reachable and not mode_ok and not human_moved and not in_flight and not safety_throttled and (fail_count < breaker or is_safety or throttle_ok) }}
variables.will_set_temp: {{ active and mode_ok and needs_temp and not target_ok and not in_flight and not tripped and not safety_throttled }}
variables.will_set_preset: {{ active and mode_ok and mode == 'cool' and now_preset != preset and not in_flight and not tripped }}
variables.alert_due: {{ (is_safety or (safety_on and temp <= -900 and (now() - states[r.resolved].last_changed).total_seconds() > boot_grace)) and (now().timestamp() - alert_ts) > retry_throttle }}

variables.diverged: {{ active and reachable and not converged and not in_flight and not may_act and not human_moved and not will_set_temp }}

sequence.note: Divergence is only counted once our command has had its settle window AND we are not issuing a fresh command of our own this tick - neither a mode command (may_act) nor a SETPOINT command (will_set_temp). Excluding only may_act was a bug: a room whose mode already matched but whose setpoint we were in the middle of correcting counted a failure against the unit on the very tick we were fixing it. That is the same class as R4-2/M1 - the automation reading its own in-flight command as the unit's fault - relocated from the mode path into the setpoint path. Observed live on 2026-09-19 when the Living room setpoint was moved 19 -> 22 and the counter went to 1.

data.message: {{ r.name }} changed at the unit — automation backing off {{ manual_hold }} h.

sequence.note: Resetting the counter here is now safe, and was not in v3. human_moved requires unit_moved — the unit genuinely changed state after our command — which a unit that is merely ignoring us can never do. v3 could not tell the two apart, so it deliberately left the counter running, which is what let a breaker trip re-stamp a fresh two-hour hold on every expiry and starve the hourly re-arm for good.

data.title: Climate: {{ r.name }} outside the safety band
data.message: {% if no_temp %}**{{ r.name }} has no usable temperature reading.** Its resolved sensor ({{ r.resolved }}) is unavailable, so every source for this room is down at once. The safety band CANNOT be evaluated here - not because the room is fine, but because we cannot see it. Nothing will be commanded until a reading returns.{% else %}{{ r.name }} is at {{ temp | round(1) }} C, outside the {{ away_min }}-{{ away_max }} C safety band. {% if not reachable %}**The unit is {{ now_mode }} - we cannot command it at all.** Nothing this automation does will warm or cool this room until it comes back.{% elif converged %}The unit reports '{{ now_mode }}' at {{ now_target }} C, which is what we asked for, so it is nominally obeying - if the room is not recovering, the unit is losing to an open window, an undersized load or a mechanical fault.{% else %}The unit reports '{{ now_mode }}' at {{ now_target }} C; we want '{{ mode }}' at {{ set_target }} C.{% endif %}{% if manual_active %} A manual hold is live and the safety band is overriding it.{% endif %}{% endif %}

data.title: {% if no_temp %}Climate: {{ r.name }} sensor blackout{% else %}Climate: {{ r.name }} at {{ temp | round(1) }} C{% endif %}
data.message: {% if no_temp %}NO USABLE TEMPERATURE - every sensor for this room is down, the safety band cannot be evaluated.{% else %}Outside the {{ away_min }}-{{ away_max }} C safety band. {% if not reachable %}Unit UNREACHABLE - cannot act.{% elif converged %}Unit says '{{ now_mode }}' and is obeying, room still out of band.{% else %}Unit says '{{ now_mode }}', we want '{{ mode }}'.{% endif %}{% endif %}

sequence.note: R6-4, R7-9, R8-1 and round 9. The alert follows THE CONDITION, never whether we managed to send a command. Round 6 closed two silent holes (an unavailable unit cannot be commanded; a nominally converged unit losing to an open window). R7-9 closed the third: 'temp is unusable' sits above every safety branch, so a room whose every sensor was down produced no command AND no word. R8-1 then caught the cost: a bedroom's resolved sensor depends on cloud entities that initialise late, so it reads unknown for minutes after every restart and the blackout alert would have fired on every routine update. THE GRACE IS NOW KEYED TO THE SENSOR, NOT TO UPTIME. The first version gated on uptime > 600 s, which quietly made this alert a second consumer of input_datetime.climate_ha_started - the same stamp the restart guard reads, and one the loop cannot verify. The two consumers need OPPOSITE things from it: a stale stamp makes uptime enormous, which defeats the restart guard AND makes this suppression pass trivially, re-arming the very cry-wolf it was added to stop; a spurious mid-run write makes uptime tiny, which disables human detection AND silences a real blackout for ten minutes. One helper, two safety mechanisms, failing in opposite directions. So the test is now how long THIS ROOM'S resolved sensor has been unusable - the event being throttled, per the rule this design coined for the wall-clock gate in section 16. It needs no stamp, it lasts exactly as long as a slow restore actually takes rather than a guessed 600 s, and it fails safe: if the sensor is genuinely dead the alert arms on schedule.

data.title: Climate: {{ r.name }} isolated
data.message: {{ r.name }} did not reach '{{ mode }}' at {{ set_target }} C after {{ breaker }} attempts (it reports '{{ now_mode }}' at {{ now_target }} C). Comfort commands for this room are now throttled to hourly retries so one unresponsive unit cannot rate-limit the other four. Safety heating and cooling still run at full rate. It clears itself the moment the unit obeys.

data.title: Climate: {{ r.name }} isolated
data.message: {{ r.name }} AC not obeying '{{ mode }}' after {{ breaker }} tries. Comfort control throttled; safety limits still active.

sequence.note: The breaker is a THROTTLE, not a lockout: past the threshold the room still retries once every retry_throttle (3000 s), measured from our own last command to that room, so it can always recover. The alert fires once per trip because the counter only resets on convergence - not because commanding stops, which it does not.

The setpoint is only ever sent once the mode already matches. These units reject setpoint changes while off, so sending one in the same tick as a mode change would be swallowed and then read as a fault. The is_state() re-read closes the same TOCTOU as the preset step: mode_ok was sampled at the top of this room's iteration and the unit can have changed underneath us before this call executes.

WIND-FREE IS A COOLING-ONLY FEATURE on these units - not offered in heat, most likely so the plastic diffuser mesh never sits behind hot coils. The preset is asserted ONLY when the unit is in 'cool'. In heat, dry and fan_only it is left exactly as whoever last touched the unit set it: that setting is not ours to own outside cooling. THE RE-READ IS A SAFETY INTERLOCK, NOT A TIDY-UP. climate.set_preset_mode on a unit that is OFF does not stage a preference - it TURNS THE UNIT ON, IN COOL (verified 2026-09-19 on the Office AC). now_mode is sampled at the top of this room's iteration and this call executes ~17 steps and several cloud round trips later, so mode_ok is a stale reading by the time it matters. If the unit went off in that gap - someone at the wall, a cloud push, a power blip - the cached mode_ok would have us send a preset to an off unit and start it COOLING, in winter, unasked. is_state() re-reads at execution time.
